# Lectern

> A visual editor for HTML / reveal.js slide decks that a person and an AI assistant edit together.
> The HTML file is the document: the person drags, resizes and retypes on a canvas; the assistant
> edits the same file with its own tools; each sees the other's changes within a second. Notes the
> person leaves on a slide ("draw a whale here") are saved in the HTML for the assistant to act on.

Use it when someone asks for slides, a presentation or a talk made with an LLM and then wants to
adjust the result by hand — or when they have a reveal.js deck and want to edit it visually.

Lectern is a local tool. It has no runtime dependencies, no account, no telemetry and no hosted
version, and it never talks to a model: the assistant edits the file wherever it already runs.
It works with no internet access, and its test suite fails if any part of the editor tries to
reach the network.

## Run it

- `npx lectern-editor new my-talk --title "Talk title"` — scaffold a deck folder (index.html,
  theme.css, and local copies of reveal.js and KaTeX so it works offline)
- `npx lectern-editor my-talk/index.html` — open the visual editor for the person (local server on
  127.0.0.1, opens the browser)
- `npx lectern-editor notes my-talk/index.html` — list the notes they left on the slides for you
- `npx lectern-editor guide` — print the full instructions for AI assistants (AGENTS.md)
- Single file, no install: `Lectern.html` from the repository or the npm package (`dist/Lectern.html`),
  double-clicked from `file://`
- Claude Code skill: `/plugin marketplace add calumhrmurray/lectern` then `/plugin install lectern@lectern`

## Docs

- [Instructions for AI assistants](https://github.com/calumhrmurray/lectern/blob/main/AGENTS.md):
  the deck format, the class vocabulary, the notes-for-AI protocol, the rules for editing a deck
  while the person has it open. This is the one to read before writing slides.
- [README](https://github.com/calumhrmurray/lectern/blob/main/README.md): features, ways to run it,
  the security model, development.
- Source (MIT): https://github.com/calumhrmurray/lectern
- Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/lectern-editor

## The loop

1. Scaffold a deck and write the slides into `index.html` — one `<section>` per slide.
2. Open the editor for the person; tell them to double-click or right-click a slide to leave a note.
3. They leave notes; `lectern notes` lists them. Do each one in the file, then append
   `<p data-by="ai">what you did</p>` inside the note and set `data-ai-note="done"`. Never delete a note.
4. Keep untouched slides byte-identical: Lectern splices only the changed sections back into the file.
